conviction_note: abs_move 11% (option-implied 9.84%, median of 7 prior reactions 8.05%, tail of 31-36%, about 22% of float short) times a mild long lean, p_up 55. The lean comes from three things: the 100 MW and 150 MW expansion leases were 'advanced' on 27 July and there has been no 8-K since; FQ1 revenue probably clears a stale bar; and a crowded short sits in a sector that fell on rates. The lean is held near 50 because this name sold or ignored its last two revenue beats (+0.93% on a 2.5x beat, -8% on a beat) and the skew pays slightly for downside. The findings sum to +2.3 against a scaled +1.1. The gap is the reaction function: each finding is sized on its own and is mostly positive, while the whole print could still go either way.
bar: Disputed. FQ1 FY27 (quarter to 2026-08-31) revenue consensus is $134.86m with adjusted EPS -$0.30 per Tiger's preview (https://www.itiger.com/news/1141164502), $118.7m with EPS -$0.20 per a webull/Zacks-sourced summary (https://www.webull.com/news/15317551320294400), and $114.7m with EPS -$0.20 per a Seeking Alpha snippet. MarketBeat shows EPS -$0.30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APLD/earnings/) and Northland -$0.06. The company gives no guidance: the FQ4 release says 'no specific outlook' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144879/000114487926000044/apldq426earningsreleaseasf.htm). The basis also differs: MarketBeat's FQ4 actual of $240.35m is revenue excluding the Cloud segment, against GAAP of $258.7m. Every finding that depends on the bar is therefore capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is 57.86m shares, 21.94% of float, 4.1 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15, down 0.97% from the prior period (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APLD/short-interest/). It peaked at 34.1% of float in January 2026. Shares outstanding were 302.3m on 2026-09-23 (POSASR). The skew is +2.23 vol points, a mild premium on downside; put/call OI is 0.73 and ATM IV 148%. The event-implied move is 9.84%. The stock is -11.7% over 20 sessions and -51.7% from its 52-week high; it was -24% in the month to 2026-09-15 on a sector-wide AI-hosting slide blamed on rate expectations. Of 20 analysts, 16 rate it Buy or Strong Buy (MarketBeat). Jones Trading initiated at Buy with a $70 target on 2026-09-28 and the stock fell 6% that day. This is a crowded short in a beaten-down name, so the squeeze is a mechanism of its own.

findings.finding: Polaris Forge 1 Building 2 Phase 2 has not been leased out to a second tenant; this finding is about the two expansion leases. On the 2026-07-27 call management said it was in advanced talks with two existing customers for about 100 MW and 150 MW of expansion, at 'materially higher rates than their current leases', and that it was marketing a further 1.7 GW. EDGAR shows no 8-K from APLD between 2026-07-27 and 2026-10-07 (only Forms 4, ARS, DEF 14A and POSASR), so neither lease had been signed and disclosed as of early October. This print is where the stock has historically moved on lease news: +31% (Jul-2025, CoreWeave), +16% (Oct-2025, PF2 talks), +8% (Jan-2026, 900 MW pipeline). When there was no new pipeline news it moved -8% and +0.9%. A signed expansion at higher rates would also answer the bear case that the 810 MW of hyperscaler leases were priced below peers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Lease and pipeline news packaged with the print: +31.01% (2025-07-30), +16.05% (2025-10-09), +8.05% (2026-01-07). Prints without new lease news: -7.99% (2026-04-08) and +0.93% (2026-07-27; the Delta Forge 2 lease had been announced on June 8 before that print).
findings.why_not_priced: Had the market expected these leases, the stock would not be 52% off its high, it would not have fallen 6% on a $70 Buy initiation, and the skew would not lean to downside. Talks first disclosed 10 weeks ago with no filing since read as stale. The two-sided risk is real: if management says on the call that the expansions slipped, the yield bear case gets stronger. The Finland site released the day before the print had no tenant (https://ir.applieddigital.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/162/applied-digital-secures-up-to-1-gw-of-potential-power), which is weak evidence that no lease was ready to headline.
findings.independence: The EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001144879&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) independently confirms that no lease 8-K has been filed since 2026-07-27. The same 100/150 MW claim also appears in trefis's 2026-09-03 article (same call, so the same source). Needham's estimate raise for 150 MW of Delta Forge expansion was cited in a webull summary, date unverified.

findings.finding: FQ1 revenue probably clears the $115-135m bar. Base rent alone should rise from $44.1m to about $65-70m: Building 1 at 100 MW for the full quarter plus Building 2 Phase 1 (75 MW, ready for service 2026-06-30) for July-August. Add about $37m of data-center hosting and about $18m of cloud. That totals about $125-135m GAAP before any tenant fit-out revenue. Fit-out revenue is lumpy and tied to deliveries: $18.9m in FQ3 and $152.4m in FQ4, booked ahead of the 2026-06-30 handover. Building 2 Phase 2 was handed over on 2026-10-02 and the Polaris Forge 2 buildings are entering fit-out, so another fit-out tranche in FQ1 is plausible. Consensus of $115-135m appears to model none.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ4 revenue of $258.7m against a consensus of about $95-104m (2.5x) bought +0.93% (2026-07-27). FQ3 revenue of $126.6m, a beat, was sold -7.99% (2026-04-08) on a wider GAAP loss. On the last two prints the name has not paid for revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: If consensus included fit-out revenue it would sit near or above FQ4's $258.7m rather than $115-135m. The market appears to treat fit-out as pass-through, at roughly 15% gross margin, which is why this finding is small.
findings.independence: FQ3 fit-out of $18.9m is in the FQ3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1144879/000114487926000029/apldq326earningsrelease.htm). The 10-K says FY26 fit-out totalled $270.6m at PF1 and that heavy construction continues through FY27 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144879/000114487926000048/apld-20260531.htm). Local reporting on 2026-09-14 says the PF2 buildings are 'approaching fit-out stage' (https://www.remio.ai/post/applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-is-rising-fast-but-its-rural-ai-bet-faces-a-publ). All three are company-derived and part of the inference.

findings.finding: GAAP EPS has missed consensus badly on two consecutive prints: FQ3 -$0.36 against -$0.13, and FQ4 -$0.39 against -$0.09 (MarketBeat). Interest on about $5.0bn of long-term debt is increasingly expensed rather than capitalised as buildings enter service, with 250 MW live by 2026-10-02. That makes a third GAAP miss against the -$0.20 to -$0.30 bar likely, while adjusted EPS (+$0.04 in FQ4) has beaten.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A GAAP miss with a wider net loss was sold -7.99% (2026-04-08). A GAAP miss of -$0.39 against -$0.09 alongside a revenue beat moved +0.93% (2026-07-27).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the trend is visible, and on the last print the market looked through it. The EPS bar itself is disputed (-$0.06 to -$0.30), so this is capped small.
findings.independence: The long-term debt of $5.0bn at 2026-05-31 comes from the FQ4 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144879/000114487926000044/apldq426earningsreleaseasf.htm). The capitalisation inference is mine.

findings.finding: Before the print the company announced that Building 2 Phase 2 at Polaris Forge 1 reached ready-for-service on 2026-10-02, taking live capacity to 250 MW of the 400 MW contracted. That is a second on-cadence handover in three months and points to an FQ2 base-rent step-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Delivery milestones are the line the name trades on alongside leases. Previews say 'capacity milestones and utilization are the leading variables for share-price reaction'. The 2026-07-01 delivery release came before a +0.93% print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since it is public. The stock still drifted lower after it, which suggests the market is not crediting execution. What the call adds is the FQ2 revenue implication and the timing of Building 3 and PF2.
findings.independence: The 10-K schedule puts PF1 Buildings 2-3 in 1H27 and PF2 in 2H26-1H27 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144879/000114487926000048/apld-20260531.htm). Local reporting on 2026-09-14 says PF2's rooftop equipment is installed and Fargo's annexation challenge was withdrawn (https://www.remio.ai/post/applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-is-rising-fast-but-its-rural-ai-bet-faces-a-publ).

findings.finding: ChronoScale (CHRN), about 96% owned and consolidated by APLD, announced on 2026-10-01 an expansion with an existing AI-infrastructure customer and a new customer agreement. It says these are projected to take annualized revenue run-rate to $1bn by Q3 2027, against APLD's total FY26 revenue of $611m and a cloud segment of about $18m a quarter. The APLD call is the first place the parent can quantify the capex and the consolidated revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with a cloud-segment surprise of this size. The May 2026 separation into CHRN did not show up as a print reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: APLD went from $24.70 on 9/28 to $23.97 today, so the $1bn run-rate target has not lifted the parent. It was released under a different ticker, and the GPU capex it needs is unquantified. If the market had credited it, APLD would have moved on 10/1-10/2. Net of the rest of the company: the GPU-cloud margin and its funding (possible CHRN equity under the S-3 filed 2026-10-06) could offset it.
findings.independence: The ChronoScale 8-K of 2026-10-02 (items 5.02/5.03/7.01) is the same document. The FQ4 release confirms APLD owns about 96% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144879/000114487926000044/apldq426earningsreleaseasf.htm).

findings.finding: Before the print the company announced up to 1 GW of potential power capacity in Finland, its first non-US site, with initial power in 2028 and no tenant yet. The CEO pre-empted it as 'a deliberate first step, not a change in our strategy'. Calls may draw questions on capex scope and focus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for international expansion. MarketBeat's news list carries a 247wallst headline saying the stock fell 4% ahead of earnings despite the Finland agreement.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since it was released the day before. What remains is how the call frames capex and whether it distracts from the US expansions.
findings.independence: This shares the inference in finding 1 that no US lease was ready to headline; I have sized it once here on the capex angle only.

findings.finding: Counterparty demand read-through. Oracle, the reported Polaris Forge 2 tenant, posted FQ1 FY27 in September 2026: RPO of $664bn, more than $30bn of new AI contracts, about 1 GW of capacity delivered in the quarter, and FY27 capex of up to $95bn. CoreWeave, the PF1 tenant, raised its 2026 guide in August to revenue of $12.4-13.2bn with backlog of $104bn. Both point to sustained hyperscaler demand for the 1.7 GW APLD is marketing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history. The sector slid through September despite these prints, so the transmission is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: Broadly public. It is a proxy for APLD and gets small weight. If it had transmitted, APLD would not be -24% in the month to 9/15 while counterparties guided up.
findings.independence: CoreWeave Q2 2026 release (https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/). The tenant identification for PF2 comes from local and press reporting (https://www.remio.ai/post/applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-is-rising-fast-but-its-rural-ai-bet-faces-a-publ).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: about 22% of float short (57.9m shares, 4.1 days, 2026-09-15) after a sector-wide AI-hosting slide attributed to rates and oil-driven inflation rather than company news. APLD was -24% in the month to 9/15 and -6% on 9/28 despite a $70 Buy initiation. Sell-side targets sit far above spot (average about $61-73).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest peaked at 34% of float in January 2026, and the January print moved +8.05%. The squeeze-prone setup has produced +16% and +31% reactions on positive pipeline news.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, so this finding is only an asymmetry: with about 22% short and the stock near its 52-week low (+16.7% above), any positive lease or guide surprise is amplified. The +2.23 skew shows the option market is not paying for that asymmetry.
findings.independence: MarketBeat short interest (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APLD/short-interest/). The 247wallst article of 2026-09-15 attributes the slide to sector repricing (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/15/terawulf-falls-5-as-ai-infrastructure-names-extend-a-month-long-slide-iren-drops-4-applied-digital-declines-3/).

findings.finding: Financing overhang, signed as zero after asking what the money buys. The POSASR filed 2026-09-25 registers about 53.1m common shares for resale, including about 24.6m from future Series G preferred conversions. The preferred equity purchase agreement (PEPA) was lifted to $2.0bn on 2026-06-26, with $835m still available and conversion floored at $34. Separately there are $1.59bn and $2.15bn of 2031 secured notes. The money funds buildings already leased for 15 years to investment-grade tenants: 250 MW live and about $36bn contracted. A new raise announced alongside the print is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Notes offerings in June 2026 and March 2026 did not stop subsequent prints from reacting to leases. The 2025-04-14 print (-35.94%) came with a cloud-business pivot and financing worry.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and registered. The $34 conversion floor against a $24 spot limits near-term conversion supply. The ramp the money funds is corroborated by deliveries and contracted leases, so it is not sized negative.
findings.independence: The 10-K liquidity statement shows $1.6bn unrestricted cash plus $2.6bn restricted at 2026-05-31 and 'sufficient liquidity... for at least the next 12 months' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144879/000114487926000048/apld-20260531.htm).

outside_window.finding: Finland site initial power is anticipated in 2028, and any tenant lease there is unscheduled.
Assignment of the PF1 Building 3 CoreWeave lease to a CoreWeave subsidiary, contingent on that subsidiary getting an investment-grade rating (MOU dated 2026-06-05). No date has been set.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider Form 4s since July: the CFO on 2026-10-04 and the President on 2026-09-12 are both F-code tax withholding on RSU vesting, with no open-market buys or sales (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1144879/000162828026065122/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1791241026.xml, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1144879/000190044526000004/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1789418949.xml)
APLD 8-Ks since 2026-07-27: none. No lease, financing or material-agreement filing in FQ1 or after it.
Company-specific negative news explaining the September drawdown: none found. Trefis (2026-09-30) says 'We found no news that explains the fall'; 247wallst attributes it to sector and rates.
PF2 community and permit opposition: Fargo withdrew its annexation attempt per the 2026-09-14 report. No delay was reported.
Delta Forge 1 (Rapides Parish, LA) construction delay news: none. Site work began January 2026, with operations targeted for mid-2027.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Analyst concern that the 810 MW of hyperscaler leases were priced at lower yields than peers (trefis, 2026-09-03)
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the expansion-lease finding: a signed expansion at 'materially higher rates' is the resolution of this concern.

rejected_candidates.detail: The story cannot be dated to 2026. CoreWeave's Q2 2026 release (August 2026) raised its guide, which contradicts it as current news (https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/).

rejected_candidates.candidate: Meta launching a cloud business to sell excess AI capacity, hitting the neoclouds
rejected_candidates.detail: July 2026 news that was priced before the FQ4 print. It is part of the sector-sentiment backdrop already carried in the positioning finding.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the positioning finding as evidence that the sell-side is not moving the stock.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly long against a mildly downside-paid skew (+2.23) and a -11.7% 20-day run-up. The positive case rests on a lease catalyst that is overdue but unconfirmed, and on a crowded short. A muted or negative reaction to a revenue beat is what this name has done twice running, which keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): the revenue and fit-out beat was cut from +0.8 to +0.4, because this name moved +0.93% on a 2.5x revenue beat and -8% on the beat before it.
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): consensus runs $114.7-134.86m on revenue and -$0.06 to -$0.30 on EPS, so the GAAP EPS miss finding was cut from -0.4 to -0.2.

Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the expansion-lease finding was cut from +1.2 to +1.0, because the no-tenant Finland pre-release and the absence of any 8-K argue partly against a lease at the print.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the PEPA resale registration and notes fund buildings already leased to investment-grade tenants, with 250 MW live, so the finding moved from -0.3 to 0.0.
Lesson 5 (proxy is small): Oracle and CoreWeave demand read-through cut from +0.3 to +0.2. Positioning cut from +0.6 to +0.4, because positioning is the information set rather than an edge.
Scaled number: p_up moved from 56 to 55 under lessons 1 and 6; abs_move_pct unchanged at 11.
